result.memory: Jules has persistent cross-session memory at the repository level. \"Jules Memory for Repositories\" (announced September 30, 2025) captures preferences, nudges, and corrections during tasks, and the next time a task runs in that repository Jules consults the saved memory to anticipate the user's needs and patterns. It is a server-side cloud feature: no file path or storage location is documented. It can be toggled per repository in the repo settings page under \"Knowledge\" (default on/off state is not documented), and its scope is explicitly per repository — the docs say memory is referenced for \"the same or a similar task in that specific repository,\" with no cross-repository carry-over described. The Gemini 3 Pro changelog entry (November 19, 2025) later refers to \"Agentic Memories,\" described as Jules using context more effectively to adapt to coding preferences over time.
result.notes:
Everything above was verified from the official Jules documentation, which currently lives at https://jules.google/docs; the URL https://developers.google.com/jules returns HTTP 404 as fetched. The docs publish a machine-readable index at https://jules.google/docs/llms.txt and a .md variant of every page.

Cloud vs local: Jules is a cloud autonomous agent — each task runs in a fresh Google-hosted virtual machine that clones the repository, and AGENTS.md is read from the repository root inside that cloud session. Jules Tools, the command-line surface, is a client for the same cloud service; the docs describe no local convention-file loading for it (no user-level ~/.jules/AGENTS.md, no local instruction config).

Not documented: nested or subdirectory AGENTS.md files (only the repository-root file is described); precedence when multiple instruction sources exist; any user-level or enterprise-level instruction/context files; compatibility with other agents' convention files — CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursor/rules, .cursor/skills, or skill directories of any kind are not mentioned anywhere in the docs, and AGENTS.md (plus README.md as a setup-hints fallback) is the only convention file Jules documents. The docs are likewise silent on the exact spelling beyond describing it as AGENTS.md (the environment page uses lowercase "agents.md").

Other context configured through the UI rather than files: environment setup scripts and per-repository environment variables are entered in repository settings, and MCP server connections are added per account on the Jules Settings page; none of these have documented config-file paths.

The foundation files product.md, tech.md, and structure.md are created here. Reference syntax #[[file:<relative_path>]] pulls live workspace files in.

Global steering applies to all workspaces; workspace steering wins conflicts. Documented as the deployment target for team-wide steering pushed by MDM or Group Policy. Kiro Web and Mobile cannot read it (no local filesystem); reuse in cloud sessions requires uploading it through Configuration Sync.

result.memory: Kiro documents two kinds of persistent agent memory. On Kiro Web, the agent keeps an automatic account-level memory: as you work and give feedback — including guidance left on pull-request reviews — it learns preferences and applies them to future work across all repositories. That memory is maintained automatically, surfaced in the Settings > Memory section of Kiro Web, can include or exclude individual learned items, and is explicitly documented for Kiro Web (cloud sessions) rather than the local surfaces. For the IDE and CLI, no separate automatic memory is documented; the persistent-context mechanism there is explicit steering files on disk, which survive across sessions by design. Separately, the open-source Kiro Crew agent ships a six-layer memory rooted at ~/.kiro/crew/workspace/memory/: preferences.md (replaced wholesale by a consolidator every 30 messages, injected into every new session), projects.md, recent history under history/*.md with a three-tier decay, SQLite-backed semantic memory (confidence-gated writes) and episodic memory tables with an optional FAISS index plus time-decay and MMR reranking, and a lessons layer where learned corrections override defaults and user-explicit lessons always win.
result.notes:
All file paths above were read from pages on kiro.dev/docs fetched during this documentation pass; each canonical page also has a markdown twin at the same URL plus .md.

Compatibility with other harnesses: Kiro's docs document support for the AGENTS.md standard and the open Agent Skills standard, and say skills can be imported from the community or other compatible AI tools — the documented mechanism imports (copies) skill packages, it does not read foreign convention directories such as .cursor/rules, .cursor/skills, or .claude/skills in place; any direct reading of those paths is not documented. CLAUDE.md support is not documented. "Import" behavior places skills under .kiro/skills/ or ~/.kiro/skills/.

Cloud vs local surfaces: Kiro is not a cloud-only agent. One agent harness runs locally on IDE and CLI and in a managed cloud sandbox for Web, Mobile, and cloud sessions created from the IDE or CLI. Cloud sessions read project configuration committed under .kiro/ in the cloned repository (steering, specs, custom agents, hooks, MCP servers, and skills) and never the local ~/.kiro directory; personal configuration reaches the cloud only through Settings > Sync, and the cloud copy can optionally be applied to new local sessions. Kiro Mobile reads project steering and skills only and uses built-in agents. Kiro Web additionally reads project MCP servers, custom agents, and hooks, and can invoke project agents as sub-agents but not as the primary session agent.

Precedence summary across scopes: steering, skills, and hooks merge across all scopes (workspace steering wins conflicts, and workspace skills take priority over same-named global skills); custom agents resolve project > global with same-name project winning; MCP servers resolve agent config > workspace mcp.json > global mcp.json; workflow recipes resolve project > global > synchronized account recipes > bundled recipes; permissions use deny-overrides with enterprise managed-settings.json outranking user rules; managed settings are client-enforced on the machine and do not apply to Kiro Web.

Additional documented paths and controls: the KIRO_HOME environment variable redirects the global ~/.kiro directory (agents, skills, steering, settings, and sessions all resolve against it). CLI settings live at ~/.kiro/settings/cli.json (global only). Agent-scope MCP, permissions, hooks, powers, steering, and skills are embedded in the agent configuration file rather than separate paths. Kiro IDE extension registry and MDM extension controls exist for VSIX tooling but no instruction content is documented in them.

result.memory: The only persistent cross-session agent memory Cursor documents is for Cloud Agent automations: each automation gets "Memories", where the agent can read and write persistent notes across runs. A memory is stored as a named entry (MEMORIES.md by default) that exists outside the agent's working filesystem, is enabled by default and can be disabled, and can be viewed, edited, or deleted from the automation's tool configuration UI. Memories are per-automation and persist across runs. For the IDE/CLI Agent, no cross-session memory store or memory file is documented (not documented).
result.notes:
Cursor's documented convention surface spans four rule types (Project Rules, User Rules, Team Rules, AGENTS.md), Agent Skills, subagents, hooks, plugins, and MCP. The built-in system prompt itself is not file-configurable: the context breakdown describes "System prompt" as Cursor's built-in instructions, while rules, skills, MCP, and subagents are separate injected categories (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting). CLAUDE.md as an instruction file is not documented anywhere in the docs; Claude compatibility appears only as read directories (.claude/skills/, .claude/agents/, ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.claude/agents/), the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable in plugin MCP configs, and the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR hook environment alias.

Cloud sessions vs local surfaces. Cloud Agents read AGENTS.md from the repository (docs recommend a "Cursor Cloud specific instructions" section), and read rules from all three levels (user, team, repo .cursor/rules/*.mdc). Project skills committed to the repo are available to cloud agents; personal skills in ~/.cursor/skills/ reach the cloud only when "Sync Skills for Cloud Agents" is enabled (only ~/.cursor/skills/ syncs - project skills, ~/.agents/skills/, and other local files stay on the machine), and self-hosted workers use project skills or skills baked into the worker image. Cloud agents run command-based hooks from <project-root>/.cursor/hooks.json plus, on Enterprise, team and enterprise-managed hooks; user-level ~/.cursor/hooks.json is not available in cloud agents, Tab hooks and workspaceOpen do not apply, and sessionEnd/sessionStart semantics differ. Docs state subagents are usable in the editor, CLI, and Cloud Agents, but which custom subagent directories cloud sessions pick up is not documented. User-level skills sync is admin-gated: Team/Enterprise admins can disable "Sync Skills for Cloud Agents" for everyone. Skills can be published to a team marketplace, which stores a Cursor-hosted copy separate from the local sync.

Precedence across categories: rules use Team -> Project -> User; hooks merge Enterprise -> Team -> Project -> User; subagents resolve project-over-user and .cursor/ over .claude//.codex/; precedence among skill directories (e.g., .cursor/skills vs .agents/skills, or project vs user skills) is not documented, and plugin-provided rules have no documented rank versus file-based rules. Also not documented: a user-level AGENTS.md (docs limit AGENTS.md to project root and subdirectories), any legacy .cursorrules support, a standalone filesystem path for user/workspace slash commands (command files are documented only inside plugins at commands/), and a memory file for the IDE/CLI agent. CLI configuration (~/.cursor/cli-config.json globally, <project>/.cursor/cli.json for permissions only) holds settings and permissions rather than instructions, so it is listed here only for completeness (https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/configuration). Plugins ship as git repositories discovered through .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json or the Cursor Marketplace; Cursor expands ${CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} but not the Agent Plugins ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/${PLUGIN_DATA} variables.

result.memory: Cascade, the legacy local agent, has persistent cross-session memory in two forms: auto-generated Memories that it stores locally in ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/ (workspace-scoped — memories made in one workspace are unavailable in another — never committed to the repository, and never shared with teammates), and user-defined Rules (global_rules.md etc.) which are the durable, shareable channel. Users can also prompt "create a memory of ..." at any time. Devin Local — the default local agent in Devin Desktop and the successor harness — does not persist memories between sessions at all; Cognition's migration path is the "Devin: Open Cascade Migration Wizard" command, which moves memories into skills. On the cloud surface, Devin sessions recall cross-session Knowledge items held in the Devin cloud (managed at app.devin.ai/settings/knowledge with repo, organization, or enterprise scoping); Knowledge is deprecated and is being migrated automatically to Skills in Plugins.
result.notes: Identity: Windsurf is mid-rebrand to Devin Desktop (Cognition). docs.windsurf.com now 308-redirects to docs.devin.ai — the getting-started page cited for this atlas (docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/getting-started) resolves to https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/getting-started. Every evidence link above is the resolved docs.devin.ai URL as fetched, and every path documented here is still read for backward compatibility (the .windsurf/ trees work side by side with .devin/). Three surfaces matter for convention files: Cascade (legacy local agent, full rules/memories/workflows support), Devin Local (default local agent for new tabs; runs the Devin CLI harness, so it reads AGENTS.md through the CLI rules system, uses the same skills discovery, supports subagents and agent plugins, but has no memories or workflows — only paths documented for the shared CLI harness apply to it), and Devin cloud sessions (delegated from the editor; read repository AGENTS.md with a 16 KiB automatic injection limit and .agents/skills, and can run plugin skills, but plugin subagents are explicitly local-only and cloud reading of repository .devin/rules or .windsurf/rules directories is not documented — say "not documented" rather than assuming). Precedence, as far as the docs state it: .devin/ is preferred over legacy .windsurf/ everywhere (for rule directories the Windsurf tree is a fallback, while for the single global_rules.md file only the .devin/ copy is loaded when both exist); root AGENTS.md is always-on while subdirectory AGENTS.md files are glob-scoped; enterprise system rules merge with, and do not override, user-defined rules. Cross-tool config import is a feature of the shared Devin CLI harness: it imports rules, skills, commands, and MCP servers from Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, .claude/commands, .claude/settings*), GitHub Copilot skills, OpenCode, and Zed — each disableable via read_config_from in ~/.config/devin/config.json or .devin/config.json (all default true); Copilot custom-instruction files and Windsurf workflows are explicitly not imported. Devin Desktop's "Claude Code config reading" setting (which enables .claude/skills scanning) is referenced on the skills page but its UI location is not documented on the pages read. Plugins: Devin agent plugins manifest as .devin-plugin/plugin.json, falling back to .claude-plugin/plugin.json (Claude plugin compatibility) then a root plugin.json; they install at the user level and can carry AGENTS.md, rules/, skills/, agents/, hooks.json, and .mcp.json. They are unrelated to the Windsurf IDE plugins (JetBrains/VS Code — now in maintenance mode), which extend the IDE rather than the agent. Paths that exist but carry no instructions and are therefore not listed as convention files: Cascade MCP config (~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json), Cascade hooks JSON (user: ~/.codeium/windsurf/hooks.json, JetBrains plugin: ~/.codeium/hooks.json, workspace: .devin/hooks.json with legacy .windsurf/hooks.json fallback, system: /etc/devin/hooks.json etc., merged system → user → workspace), and the Devin Local agent config files (.devin/config.json, .devin/config.local.json, ~/.config/devin/config.json). Not documented anywhere in these docs: any Codex-specific convention paths (Codex appears only in agent-handoff pages, not config import) and cloud-session handling of .devin/rules or .windsurf/rules.

result.memory: Devin has persistent cross-session memory on its cloud surface, in several account-scoped forms. Knowledge (Settings > Resources > Knowledge) is a bank of tips, instructions, and documentation that Devin recalls automatically when a session's work matches an item's trigger description; items are scoped to repositories, organizations, or the enterprise, and can carry macros. Knowledge is deprecated and is being migrated automatically to skills in plugins, with skills the recommended replacement. Devin additionally auto-generates repository Knowledge from READMEs and file structure of connected repos, and auto-pulls and updates Knowledge from specialized repository files (.rules, .mdc, .cursorrules, .windsurf, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md). A second cloud mechanism is the Automations scratchpad: a persistent document shared by a monitor automation and its child sub-devins that accumulates context across runs and acts as the automation's long-term memory. Cloud sessions themselves persist server-side and can be resumed later (devin --cloud -r). On the local surface, the Devin CLI documents no separate agent-memory store; durable context lives in rule and skill files, and local sessions persist only as resumable conversations (devin --continue, devin -r). In Devin Desktop, the legacy Cascade agent stores auto-generated memories locally in ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/ (workspace-scoped, machine-local, never committed), while the Devin Local agent — the default — does not persist memories, and the docs advise migrating relied-upon Cascade memories to skills. For cloud sessions, cross-session memory therefore lives in the Devin account (Knowledge, plugins/skills at personal, organization, or enterprise scope) rather than in the repository, except where skills are committed to the repo as files.
result.notes: Devin spans four documented surfaces: cloud sessions (app.devin.ai virtual machines), the Devin CLI in the terminal, Devin Desktop (which ships two agents — Devin Local, which is the Devin CLI harness, and the legacy Cascade agent), and Devin Review (cloud PR review). Convention-file support differs by surface and the atlas entries above mark each path accordingly. Cloud sessions load instruction context from repository AGENTS.md files (16 KiB per file, auto-injected) and discover skills from six directories scanned in every connected repository (.agents/skills, .devin/skills, .github/skills, .claude/skills, .cognition/skills, .windsurf/skills); indexed repos make skills available before cloning, and disk-scanned skills from a clone override matching indexed skills. Docs do not state that cloud sessions directly read CLAUDE.md, .devin/rules, .cursor/rules, or other local tool rule files — those reach the cloud only through Knowledge auto-pull (deprecated) and Devin Review's review-context list, so claims of direct cloud reading would be unsupported. The CLI is where the broad interop lives: it reads AGENTS.md, AGENTS.local.md, AGENT.md, .windsurfrules, and CLAUDE.md identically as always-on rules, native .devin/rules with trigger frontmatter, .devin/global_rules.md (which shadows .windsurf/global_rules.md), and it imports other tools' configuration by default under seven read_config_from keys (agents_standard, cursor, windsurf, claude, copilot, opencode, zed — all default true), covering Cursor rules and MCP, Windsurf rules/skills/MCP, Claude Code rules, skills, commands-as-skills, custom subagents and hooks, Copilot skills (read in place, since they use the same SKILL.md format), OpenCode MCP (with schema conversion), and Zed MCP (context_servers key). Plugin subagents and plugin hooks load only in local Devin agents (CLI and Devin Desktop), not in cloud sessions, and plugin hooks are documented as best-effort and fail-open. Two explicit exclusions are worth recording: Windsurf workflows (.windsurf/workflows/ and ~/.codeium/<channel>/global_workflows/) are not imported as skills, and GitHub Copilot custom instructions (.github/copilot-instructions.md and .github/instructions/*.instructions.md) are not imported. Cross-session instructions can also live outside files entirely in the cloud account: Knowledge items, Playbooks (reusable prompts that are cloud-only, not available in the CLI), and organization-defined slash commands that expand into predefined prompt templates — these are stored in Devin, not in the repository. Plugin-based instruction files (an always-on AGENTS.md at the plugin root plus rules/*.md with trigger frontmatter) are injected in every session where the plugin is installed, and plugin install authority ranks Enterprise manifest > Org manifest > repository .devin/config.json lists > user installs. For enterprise-managed local use, the CLI's system.json pins auth and proxy settings machine-wide at /etc/devin/system.json (Linux), /Library/Application Support/Devin/system.json (macOS), and C:\\ProgramData\\Devin\\system.json (Windows); no equivalent enterprise instruction-file mechanism for cloud sessions is documented. Where docs are silent, this atlas says so rather than guessing: no precedence order is stated among multiple competing always-on rule files (they are loaded together, with only .devin-vs-.windsurf global_rules.md shadowing documented), no finer path than "the .claude/ directory" is given for Claude Code custom-subagent import, and the ordering among Devin Review's default instruction files is unspecified.
